A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoQuIR and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–B, and the checklist. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a complete comparison, including code embedded in Figure 2.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 23 retrievers in Tables 2–3, quality-aware fine-tuning results in Figure 4, and downstream code-generation experiments in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, fine-tuning, and downstream experimental results, together with the analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The contrastive training-data construction and retriever fine-tuning procedure in Section 5.1 are unchanged. Figure 2 edits concern illustrative code snippets rather than the proposed retrieval method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven benchmark datasets, programming-language coverage, training-data sources, and downstream security and maintainability scenarios. The revised illustration does not establish a change to evaluated data.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same 23 retrievers. The fine-tuning and downstream comparisons in Section 5.2 also retain the same models and comparison variants.

E3.justification: Dataset construction rules, evaluation metrics, model configurations, training settings, and downstream testing procedures are unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix B, including top-5 retrieval for generation.

E4.justification: The efficiency case in Figure 2(c) changes 'ans = max(...)' to 'max_candy = max(...)', correcting an inconsistency between the updated and printed variables. This is a limited revision to an illustrative case; the language, metric-correlation, and instruction-sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 retains three independent downstream runs, and Figure 5 retains the same error bars. Checklist edits concerning statistical significance only rephrase existing statements; no statistical procedure or reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and the performance and analysis plots report identical scores, rankings, trends, and downstream outcomes. Figure 2's code correction does not introduce a new measured result or change its quality label.

T1.justification: The PPA and MRS definitions in Equations 1–2 and the complexity reasoning in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, four quality dimensions, proposed metrics, findings about retriever weaknesses, and claims about quality-aware training.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability limits are unchanged, including the CVEFixes leakage or memorization concern in Appendix B.5 and the limitations on language and quality-dimension coverage. Appendix A.2 retains its example explanations.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, synthesis and retrieval prompts, training hyperparameters, and code/data access information remain unchanged. Checklist item 5 rewords the existing release statement without changing the disclosed resources or access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed, and the positioning relative to existing retrieval benchmarks remains the same.

P1.justification: The byline changes 'Walter Pretschner' to 'Alexander Pretschner'. Local grammar, punctuation, and phrasing edits appear in the NeurIPS checklist; the research narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2's code panels are reformatted with different typography, spacing, line numbering, and adjusted highlights. Other figures and tables are visually unchanged; byline and checklist edits cause limited text reflow.

improvement.justification: Figure 2(c) now updates the accumulator it prints, removing a specific inconsistency from the efficiency illustration, while checklist wording receives modest grammatical polish. The overall gain is limited because the methods, experimental evidence, substantive explanations, and limitations remain unchanged.
